summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman was admitted to the psychiatry service after an outburst in which she threw a table during a period of emotional dysregulation. She has a history of bipolar disorder, borderline personality disorder, chronic pain from endometriosis, and substance use involving alcohol, opioids, and sedatives. During her 15-day admission, she was restarted on lamotrigine and initiated on naltrexone to support mood stabilization and reduce cravings. Electroconvulsive therapy was resumed and administered three times weekly with improvement in mood and affect. She engaged in dialectical behavior therapy, improved adherence to levothyroxine, and developed a crisis plan. By discharge, she denied suicidal ideation, demonstrated use of coping skills, and was transitioned to outpatient ECT and intensive therapy with close follow-up.
